findings.trigger: A valid append makes the serialized canonical source exceed 67,108,864 bytes.
findings.impact: The write path can accept the whole source while later managed resolution refuses that same source under its read cap; inventory-wide resolution can therefore be affected. No outage/data-loss/timing claim.
findings.smallest_alternative: Define coherent serialized pre-acceptance capacity with typed refusal before acknowledgement/effects plus an existing-oversize operator path, or use bounded/indexed/streaming authority. Do not truncate or merely raise the constant.

findings.classification: session-mode journal enumeration capacity contract gap
findings.trigger: The retained `.session-mode/journals` directory grows beyond 4096 names.
findings.impact: Directory enumeration fails before suffix filtering, while ordinary resolution scans retained journals; accumulated proof can deny resolution. No deployed incidence or outage claim.
findings.smallest_alternative: Use a crash-safe pending/current index with rebuild semantics or an explicit proof-retention/capacity contract. Never silently delete proof to fit the cap.

findings.impact: Cache hits re-resolve mode bindings, handle lookup scans/repairs all session metadata, canonical append rewrites the whole source, and artifact range reads hash/validate the full blob.
findings.smallest_alternative: Consider exact-target bindings and pending-transition/handle indexes under the same leases/CAS/recreate semantics; preserve full integrity checks where required. No generic persistence framework or measured-speed claim.

findings.confidence: source-established duplicate representation; retirement contract unresolved
findings.impact: Published canonical text is duplicated into an immutable private blob and later rematerializable from canonical source, creating separate quota/install/recovery machinery.
findings.smallest_alternative: Evaluate a source-backed opaque text/range reader only if it preserves opaque IDs≠access, current policy, exact provenance/source receipts, direct-child grants/handoff, checkpoint proof, UTF-8 byte-range semantics and export/backup/migration compatibility.

findings.classification: conditional legacy recovery isolation / retirement candidate
findings.confidence: high current fail-closed semantics; retirement obligations unresolved
findings.impact: The offline recovery path deliberately reopens/revalidates stages, retains uncertain residues and historical seals, and separates receipt finalization; complexity is real but currently protects compatibility and non-replay guarantees.
findings.smallest_alternative: Keep the recovery path isolated/lazy and retire only after D4 proves external/old-state obligations. Do not replace fail-closed residues with startup repair or lossy compatibility success.

findings.confidence: high dormancy; not a production performance defect
findings.impact: A substantial bounded idle compaction/scanner/lifecycle stack exists while activation is explicitly refused and transport/retry/finite-cleanup qualification is deferred.
findings.smallest_alternative: After consumer proof, either retire dormant scheduling/registry/transport machinery while retaining reusable checkpoint/CAS/fold logic, or integrate it through one scheduler with real transport and budget qualification.
